feedback: Approved to race. The candidate changes one field from iteration 2: controller.kd goes from 0.2 to 0.4, with ki 0.5, base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, sensors at x = ±0.05 and last_direction unchanged. Every raced design so far has ended off_track with 0 finishes. Iteration 0 (base_speed 1.6, kp 2.0, kd 0.05, sensors at ±0.04) gave max_error 0.0609 to 0.0614 and progress 0.035 to 0.115. Iteration 1 (base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, kd 0.2, ki 0) gave max_error 0.0609 to 0.0645. Iteration 2 (ki 0.5) gave essentially identical numbers, so the integral term had no measurable effect. Across these changes max_error stayed in a 0.061 to 0.065 band, just past the 0.06 m limit. Steering_oscillation stayed low (0.064 to 0.141), so jitter is not the problem. Progress (0.04 to 0.15) shows the robot leaves the line early in each run. The raced evidence therefore points to a start transient or first-bend departure, not to speed, proportional gain, derivative damping or integral bias. This candidate is a cheap, bounded test of the rate-damping part of that hypothesis, and it keeps the geometry that produced the best score so far. Approve it so the race returns per-track telemetry (max_error, progress, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and distance before the first off-track event). Read it in this order. (1) If max_error falls clearly below 0.06 on the oval and s-bend with progress above 0.2, keep kd near 0.4 and raise base_speed in steps of 0.2. (2) If max_error is unchanged near 0.061 to 0.065 on all tracks, kd is not the lever, so the next test should move the sensors forward (y 0.07) or widen the footprint (sensor_size 0.016) to give earlier steering lead. (3) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 or max_error gets worse, kd 0.4 is too high, so return to kd 0.2 and change only the sensor footprint.
requested_changes: If max_error is unchanged (about 0.061 to 0.065) on all tracks with kd 0.4, keep kd 0.4 and change geometry.sensor_positions y from 0.05 to 0.07 (sensors further ahead of the axle) to give earlier steering lead, since iterations 0 to 2 showed max_error fixed near 0.061 whatever kp, kd, ki or base_speed were.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 with kd 0.4, or max_error increases on the s-bend or slalom, return controller.kd to 0.2 and instead try geometry.sensor_size 0.016 with the same sensor positions, since kd 0.05 to 0.2 in iterations 0 to 1 gave no clear gain.

If max_error falls below 0.055 on the oval and s-bend with progress above 0.2, keep kd 0.4 and raise controller.base_speed in steps of 0.2 (1.2 to 1.4). Lower speed gave more progress in iterations 0 to 1 (0.04 at 1.6 against 0.15 at 1.2), so check progress before raising speed.
